label: End of original input / <DEL> step (strongest on y, 0 inputs; letter-initial sequences)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original and delimiter phases. Its activity is essentially zero in the copy phase (0.8% of mass). The <DEL> step holds 53% of the mass (31% of DEL steps are active). The other 47% comes from late original-phase steps (t>=3, mostly t=4-9), and these are nearly always first occurrences of the input token (in_first=1 carries 94% of the mass). Inputs y (4x lift) and 0 (2x) are the strongest. It is modulated by the first token of the sequence: rates are about 2.7x when it starts with a, p or k, then o, f, r, u, d, and lower for digit-initial sequences. It also runs slightly higher for longer L and fewer digits. It does not fire at t=0, rarely fires at t=1-2, and does not fire on repeated tokens. Activations come in runs over the last few original tokens and continue into <DEL>, which suggests a slowly built state rather than a per-token trigger, so no simple predicate captures it (dev F1 about 0.47, mass recall 0.69).
